method: Read the official TSV objects at pinned Google Cloud Storage generations. Resolve each target by MID, count matching rows as annotation events and distinct clip_id values as excerpts. No audio was downloaded or used for these counts.

evaluatedTargets.strongDisplayName: Vehicle horn, car horn, honking, toot
evaluatedTargets.mappingNote: Display names differ despite sharing the same MID. Dataset mappings must use MID rather than comparing label strings or integer class indices across resources.

scopeAndLimitations: Counts apply only to the exact continuous-time evaluation TSV version above, not to all AudioSet resources, training data, or the separate 960 ms framed positive/negative subset.

Annotation row count is not unique source count, unique recording count, or number of presently downloadable audio files. A clip can contain several events and more than one target class, so per-class clip counts must not be summed as a dataset-wide unique total.
The official strong release covers 456 distinct MIDs; it is not the same vocabulary as the original 527-class AudioSet classification release. This check confirms coverage of these four MIDs only.

Within audioset_eval_strong.tsv, event start/end offsets are relative to the annotated 10-second excerpt. The clip_id contains the parent YouTube ID and excerpt start in milliseconds; these must not be confused with the event offsets.
A timestamp annotation does not establish a universal event-boundary error bound such as 0.1 seconds, and it does not make SoundTest's classification-window event estimates precise SED boundaries.

These metadata have the official CC BY 4.0 release terms. This does not grant rights to redistribute arbitrary source YouTube audio; audio availability and applicable source permissions require separate verification.

Future evaluation must keep threshold-tuning material separate from final evaluation and check for overlap with model training/fine-tuning sources. These counts do not establish independence from a model's training corpus.
